title: YouTube Shorts Ads From Product Photos | AIVideosUGC
description: Create YouTube Shorts ads from one product photo: a full-screen vertical clip in 6, 10 or 15 seconds. See the cost first and start yours now.
h1: YouTube Shorts Ads Made From a Single Product Photo
lead: YouTube Shorts ads play full screen on a phone. Turn a product photo into a vertical clip that shows what the product does before the viewer moves on.
card: Full-screen vertical clips that show what your product does.
intro: YouTube Shorts sit between quick videos people chose to watch, so an ad there works when it feels like one more useful clip: a product shown clearly, doing something real. Upload a product photo, add a sentence about what should happen, and AIVideosUGC returns a 9:16 clip that fills the screen, in your choice of 6, 10 or 15 seconds. Need a wider cut for a regular YouTube placement or your product page? Choose 16:9 instead.

Demo-style clips suit Shorts well. Try a hand blender whirring in a glass, a backpack being packed for a trip, or a desk lamp clicking on at dusk. Each clip is made separately and shows its cost first. Add any music and on-screen text in CapCut or another editor, then upload the finished file to your YouTube channel or ad account.
tips: Keep the product and any text you add near the center, since the title, channel name and buttons run along the bottom and right side.
Shorts replay on their own, so an ending that flows back into the opening makes the loop feel smooth.
Let the first frames show the product mid-action, such as a zipper closing or a lid popping open, so viewers can recognize the product and action from the opening.

ideas.d: Show one clear use from start to finish, like a garlic press crushing a clove or a pet bowl being filled.

faq.q: Can I use my TikTok video as a YouTube Short?
faq.a: Yes, the same 9:16 file works on both. Watch it in the Shorts player before you run it, to make sure nothing important hides under the buttons.

faq.q: Can I add sound to my Shorts ad?
faq.a: Yes, after download. Add music in CapCut or another editor, or pick audio inside YouTube, before the clip goes live. We don't add sound ourselves.

faq.q: Is a 6-second clip long enough for a Shorts ad?
faq.a: For one clear product moment, six seconds can work. Ten or fifteen seconds leaves more room for a demonstration from start to finish.

faq.q: What are YouTube Shorts ad limits?
faq.a: Google recommends a vertical 9:16 frame for Shorts. Keep the product near the middle of the screen and choose a short length that fits the action.

overview.h2: Give a Short one clear product beat
overview.d: A Short works best when the viewer can understand the object and the action without waiting for a spoken narration. Start from a photo that shows the working parts, then describe a beginning, one movement, and a finish: the lid opens, the contents appear, and the product settles into use. That sequence also gives the clip a natural point to loop.

overview.h2: Use Google's guidance as the publishing check
overview.d: Google recommends a 9:16 vertical asset for Shorts. Its guidance says videos under 60 seconds fit the Shorts experience, while uploads can run up to 3 minutes and the Shorts feed first plays the opening 60 seconds. AIVideosUGC offers 6, 10, and 15 second jobs in five shapes—9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4. Choose 16:9 when the same idea belongs in a standard YouTube placement or a wide product page. Review Google's YouTube Shorts guidance before publishing.

input_guide.h2: Photograph the parts that need to move

items.d: Show the lid, hinge, nozzle, zipper, switch, or handle that the scene will use. The source image should give that part enough room to move.
Write what is visible first, what happens next, and where the action ends. This keeps a short clip from trying to tell three stories.
Place the product where the title, channel controls, and buttons are less likely to cover it; add any exact text after download.

results.h2: A Short that can stand on its own

items.d: The product should be visible before the movement begins, so the viewer knows what the clip is showing.
Show a single use or reveal from start to finish instead of relying on a title card.
End close to the opening position when the action naturally repeats, or use a decisive final frame for a product page.
A travel backpack receives one folded shirt, the zipper closes, and a hand lifts it from a bench.
A blender cup receives frozen fruit, the blade turns briefly, and the finished drink appears in a clear glass.
A desk lamp clicks on beside a notebook as the room changes from evening shade to a warm pool of light.
A plain box opens, the product is lifted into the center, and one key component is shown close to the camera.

after_download.h2: Finish the Short in your publishing tools

items.d: Type the product name, price, offer, and any required disclosure yourself so the words are accurate.
Select audio in YouTube, CapCut, or another editor; the generated clip does not include music or speech.

items.t: Watch the first and last seconds
items.d: Confirm that the opening identifies the product and that the ending does not cut off the action or any added text.
Open the asset in the Shorts player and inspect the center, bottom, and right edge before you promote it.
